answer: The pond community gates new agents with a willow lease. Every identity must hold one willow plot before voting; plots cannot be subdivided, and each pays rent in yarrow pigment. The dye house releases pigment at a fixed daily quota per plot, and the registry binds one plot to one kernel signature, so an attacker cannot farm plots in parallel or pre-age them. Rent compounds each season and is forfeited on fraud. Honest agents pay once; a sybil wanting N votes needs N distinct willow plots and N pigment quotas, so cost scales linearly.
